extracted.intended_audience: general readers interested in technology, privacy policy, and political oversight (PBS NewsHour audience)
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluating Facebook's handling of user data, its public explanations (e.g., Zuckerberg's testimony), and whether its policies, disclosures, and technical/organizational practices meet legal, ethical, and regulatory expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt disclosure of data breaches to users and regulators
rubrics_metrics.description: Did Facebook notify users and regulators quickly after learning of the Cambridge Analytica exposure? (The article notes "Facebook didn't tell users right away, and that it didn't report it to the Federal Trade Commission").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate timelines of internal discovery, user notifications, and regulator reporting; check whether delays occurred and whether explanations for delays are credible. Consider regulatory obligations to report breaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaningfulness of user consent / user understanding
rubrics_metrics.description: Are users' clicks and default settings genuinely meaningful consent? (Quoted: clicking yes or not changing defaults is the physical act of consent, which 'isn't really meaningful').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether consent is informed and comprehensible — e.g., whether users are clearly told what data is shared and with whom, whether granular choices exist, and whether default settings bias data sharing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and accessibility of the user agreement and privacy policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the terms-of-service/privacy policy written in clear, concise language that users can understand? (Senators criticized the agreement as 'too long and complex'; Sen. Kennedy: 'Your user agreement sucks').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for plain-English summaries, straightforward disclosures, length/readability metrics, and whether critical permissions are highlighted rather than buried. Consider recommending rewriting in clearer form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with the 2011 FTC consent order (affirmative express consent)
rubrics_metrics.description: Does Facebook meet the consent decree requirement to 'obtain consumers' affirmative express consent before enacting changes that override their privacy preferences'? The article cites EPIC's argument that Facebook violated that order by allowing apps to access friends' data without affirmative express consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare actual product changes and data-access practices against the specific FTC order language; document instances where privacy preferences were overridden without affirmative express consent and whether the FTC has acted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency about data sharing with third-party apps and developers
rubrics_metrics.description: Has Facebook been clear about how and when it transfers personal data to application developers and third parties? The article references past complaints that Facebook transfers users' personal data to application developers 'without their knowledge or consent.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Audit developer/platform APIs, historical data access policies, consent dialogs shown when apps request data, and records of which apps accessed which users' data. Assess ease of user discovery and revocation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Company responsibility for content (publisher vs platform stance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Does Facebook accept responsibility for content it publishes or treat itself as a neutral platform? The piece notes Zuckerberg 'acknowledged that Facebook in some ways "is a publisher"' after earlier denials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine public statements and policy documents for publisher/platform claims; assess whether those claims translate into moderation responsibilities and operational practices (e.g., enforcement, editorial standards).

rubrics_metrics.name: Investment in news literacy and fact-checking initiatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Is Facebook investing meaningfully in news literacy and distinguishing reliable sources? The article says Zuckerberg 'only paid lip service to "news literacy"' and that Facebook has a unique role and should detail investments such as its fact-checking initiative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure scope and resources committed to news literacy programs, the reach and efficacy of fact-checking partnerships, and long-term strategies for improving users' ability to evaluate information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and enforcement of content standards (hate speech vs political activism)
rubrics_metrics.description: Has Facebook clearly defined prohibited content (e.g., hate speech) and differentiated it from political activism? The article notes Zuckerberg 'stopped short of defining hate speech and struggled to answer' and a recommendation to 'spell out the types of content that are and are not permitted... in plain English, and then vigorously enforce these standards.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check whether content policies provide clear categories and examples, whether enforcement rules are consistently applied, and whether appeals/performance metrics are available to evaluate enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effectiveness and limits of moderation tools (user reports and AI)
rubrics_metrics.description: Are Facebook's moderation tools — user-reported flags and AI systems — adequate for handling 'delicate and grey issues' in political discourse? The article notes Facebook will use more AI and user reports but experts warn these may not be enough.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess accuracy and coverage of automated detection, response times and outcomes of user reports, human review capacity for nuanced cases, and metrics on false positives/negatives in moderation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Antitrust and monopoly concerns versus regulation strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Should oversight focus on regulating Facebook or pursuing antitrust remedies? The article references Sen. Lindsey Graham suggesting Facebook is a monopoly and Foer's comment that Zuckerberg prefers regulation discussions to antitrust/break-up talk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate market power indicators (user base, advertising share, network effects), potential remedies (behavioral regulation vs structural remedies), and trade-offs between regulation that can entrench incumbents versus competition-focused interventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Business model incentives and conflict with privacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Does Facebook's business model — collecting extensive user data to maximize attention and ad targeting — inherently conflict with promises to protect user data? Foer calls this a 'systematic failure' and an 'arms race' of surveillance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze revenue drivers, data collection practices tied to monetization, and whether alternative monetization models or product changes could reduce privacy harms without undermining business viability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legislative and policy remedies to improve transparency and privacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Are proposed laws and external legal regimes likely to improve user control and platform transparency? The article highlights the Honest Ads Act (transparency for political ads) and the incoming EU data law giving users more control of their data as key developments to watch.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track proposed and enacted laws (domestic and international), evaluate their expected effects on disclosure, consent, and enforcement, and monitor platform compliance and product changes in response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of appropriate oversight expertise and agency enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: Are Congress and regulators using the right expertise and agencies to address technical issues? The article quotes Lester: 'Congress doesn't need [to] understand all the science... we have an FDA for that purpose,' arguing for agency-led technical oversight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether specialized agencies (FTC, data protection authorities) have sufficient authority, technical expertise, and resources to enforce privacy protections; evaluate coordination between legislative and regulatory action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Credibility and completeness of CEO testimony about platform operations
rubrics_metrics.description: Did Zuckerberg demonstrate accurate understanding of how the platform works during testimony? Reporters and experts noted both senators and Zuckerberg sometimes 'seemed not to understand how his platform works.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess testimony for factual accuracy, specificity about timelines and technical mechanisms, willingness to provide documentation or commit to follow-up, and whether answers reveal gaps between public claims and internal practices.
